sections.h2: What makes Smyrna a distinct place to sell a house?
sections.html:
Smyrna is a compact Cobb County city of 15.4 square miles, about 16 miles from downtown Atlanta and just west of where I-285 meets I-75 at Cumberland. The city also sends its own property tax bill, separate from the one issued by the county.

Settlers arrived in 1832, a camp-meeting ground made the area a popular stop in the late 1830s, and the Western and Atlantic Railroad reached it in 1842. The city was incorporated as Smyrna in 1872. Two Civil War battles took place here on July 4, 1864. Growth jumped after Lockheed reopened the nearby Bell Bomber plant in 1951, taking the population from 2,005 in 1950 to almost 20,000 by 1970.

The 2020 census counted 55,663 residents in 24,600 households, with 26,415 housing units of which 6.9 percent were vacant. The median age was 35.4. Smyrna is nicknamed the Jonquil City for the flowers that bloom along its streets each spring.

sections.h2: How has redevelopment changed Smyrna housing?
sections.html:
Smyrna has remade its center and many older blocks since the early 1990s, and that history matters if you own an older single-family house.

  • The city began the Market Village project in 1991 to build a defined downtown with a community center, a library and a mixed retail and residential district around a fountain square.
  • Thousands of new homes, mostly cluster homes, townhouses and condominiums, replaced older neighborhoods.
  • The Silver Comet Trail ends in Smyrna, and a 2019 gift of $6 million to the PATH Foundation funded a link toward the Atlanta Beltline.
  • The city runs its own public library, the only one in Cobb County outside the county library system.

Smyrna borders Vinings to the east, Marietta to the north and west, and Mableton to the south and southwest. Before you accept the first offer on an older house, ask a local agent what recent sales on your street looked like.

sections.h2: Which roads and schools should I mention to Smyrna buyers?
sections.html:
Cobb Parkway (U.S. 41), Atlanta Road, South Cobb Drive (State Route 280) and I-285 pass through the city, and both CobbLinc and MARTA buses stop there. Buyers who commute to Cumberland, the Cobb Galleria or Midtown will care about how many minutes each trip takes, so give honest times.

Public schools belong to the Cobb County School District, and 12 of its schools serve Smyrna students. The largest by enrollment include Campbell High School, Campbell Middle School and Nickajack Elementary. Private options inside the city limits include St. Benedict's Episcopal School, Covenant Christian School and Whitefield Academy.

The terrain is typical Georgia Piedmont, with hills, broad ridges and narrow valleys, so sellers should be ready to describe any grading, drainage or retaining wall work done on the lot.

sections.h2: What permits does Smyrna require, and what do they cost?
sections.html:
All building and standalone permit applications are submitted through the city's online portal, and in-person submittals are no longer accepted. Permits are good for six months if no activity occurs, according to the city's building division.

The city's fee page lists the following charges for building permits:

City of Smyrna building permit fees as published by the Community Development Department
FeeAmount printed by the city
Building or land disturbance permit$7 per $1,000 of estimated construction cost
Records fee10 percent of the building permit fee
Standalone or MEP permit$50
Technology fee$15
Minimum building permit$125
Reinspection$50, then $100, $150 and $200 for the fourth and later

The city also says permit and water connection fees can be reduced or waived for projects approved under its development incentive program. Call the building division before starting a repair if you are unsure which category applies.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Smyrna house that had short-term renters?
sections.html:
Yes, and the license record should be in order first. Every short-term rental within Smyrna limits needs both a Short-Term Rental License and an Occupational Tax Certificate, and the application goes through the city's online portal.

The city's business license page lists what an applicant must supply:

  • Proof of liability insurance
  • A code compliance verification form
  • A short-term rental agent form
  • Proof of ownership
  • For owner-occupied houses, a homestead exemption or an affidavit in lieu of one

Contact the Business License Coordinator at 678-631-5363 to ask whether a license can move to a buyer or must be reissued. If the rental ran without a license, resolve that with the city before listing, because a buyer's attorney can search for open compliance issues.

sections.h2: How do Smyrna city taxes and Cobb County taxes fit together?
sections.html:
A Smyrna homeowner receives two property tax bills: one from Cobb County and one from the City of Smyrna. The county's assessors set the value, which Georgia law taxes at 40 percent. For 2026, Cobb mailed notices on June 5, allowed 45 days from the notice date to appeal, and set a homestead filing deadline of July 20. The county said it would mail tax bills around August 15 with payment due around October 15.

The city bills separately. The city's finance page says bills go out in September and are due in November, and that exemptions available through the city include a $10,000 exemption for owners aged 62 or over, a $22,000 exemption for owners with a 100 percent disability and limited income, and a homestead exemption that caps the city tax at the home's initial assessed value. City exemption paperwork is filed by April 1 at City Hall, 2800 King Street SE.

If city taxes go unpaid, the city says it records a FIFA lien with the Cobb Superior Court clerk, which lets it collect before the property can be sold. The county tax commissioner does not prorate taxes between seller and buyer, and its office says liability is set at closing, so the contract and settlement statement decide who pays what.

sections.h2: What if I owe taxes or need to move a deed in Smyrna?
sections.html:
Cobb County's tax commissioner accepts partial payments, and late county taxes accrue a 5 percent penalty plus monthly interest after the due date. Owners who appeal must still pay at least the appeal amount by the due date to avoid that penalty.

For the deed itself, the county office describes four common types: a recorded warranty deed, a quitclaim deed, a deed of assent used for inherited property, and an executor's deed. All must be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court. If you inherited the house or are transferring it between family members, talk to an attorney before choosing the form.

On the state level, Georgia's transfer tax is paid by the seller unless the contract shifts it, at the rate the Department of Revenue prints: $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100.

Owners with a tight deadline can weigh a standard listing against an as-is investor offer or a direct cash sale, and should compare what each leaves after taxes, liens and fees.

faqs.q: Does the City of Smyrna bill its own property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's finance department issues its own bills in September, due in November, in addition to the Cobb County bill.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Cobb County value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date shown on the notice of assessment. For 2026 the county mailed notices on June 5.

faqs.q: Do I need a license for a short-term rental in Smyrna?
faqs.a: Yes. A Short-Term Rental License and an Occupational Tax Certificate are both required, and applicants supply liability insurance proof, an agent form and proof of ownership.

faqs.q: What is the cost of a building permit in Smyrna?
faqs.a: The city prints $7 per $1,000 of estimated construction cost, with a $125 minimum building permit. Technology, records and reinspection fees are listed separately.

faqs.q: Does the county prorate taxes at closing?
faqs.a: No. The Cobb tax commissioner does not prorate between seller and buyer, so the sales contract and settlement statement decide who pays.
